column1: Relative volume of complaints per service per 100,000 customers: Q4 2010 - Q1 2026, by quarter

Note: Due to a change in methodology in November 2019, the industry average figures for pay TV complaints per 100,000 subscribers prior to Q2 2018 should not be considered comparable to those from Q2 2018.

Note: The pay-monthly mobile industry average from Q4 2019 should not be compared with the industry average prior to Q4 2019. This follows a methodological data improvement, made in agreement with Ofcom, to how Vodafone records consumer and business tariff subscribers.

Note: BT TV rebranded to EE TV in late 2023 and BT Mobile is no longer offered to new customers. In Q2 2024, we continued to receive complaints about both services. For BT bundles, we have allocated complaints to BT services, apart from Pay-TV complaints, which we have allocated to EE TV.
Landline complaints per 100,000 customers/connections: Q4 2010 - Q1 2026, by quarter

Note: For Q1 2026, the actual measurable difference between the following landline providers' number of complaints per 100,000 customers was less than one and so their figures should be considered comparable:  1. Vodafone, Sky, Virgin Media, Utility Warehouse and EE;  2. Virgin Media, Utility Warehouse, EE and Industry Average;  3. NOW Broadband and BT; 4. TalkTalk and Plusnet.

Note: In Q1 2025 TalkTalk’s Q4 2023 landline subscriber figure was corrected. This resulted in a small decrease in TalkTalk’s complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 9 to 8. This did not change TalkTalk’s position or comparability with other providers.

Note: In Q2 2024, Vodafone resubmitted its landline subscriber figures for Q3 2023 and Q1 2024. In Q3 2023, this led to a small increase in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers and although the rounded overall number stayed static at 7, it moved down one position to be behind BT and as well as remaining comparable to Plusnet and BT, became comparable to BT and Shell Energy. In Q1 2024, this led to a small increase in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers, its rounded overall number stayed static at 5, it remained in the same position, and it remained comparable to the same providers.

Note: Shell Energy purchased Post Office's telephony and broadband business in March 2021. From Q2 2021 onwards, complaints statistics for Shell Energy include complaints from a number of former Post Office customers who are served by Shell Energy.

Note: In Q4 2025, TalkTalk and Utility Warehouse's Q3 2025 landline subscriber figures were corrected. This resulted in a small decrease in TalkTalk's complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 7 to 6. This did not change TalkTalk and Utility Warehouse's position. However it did affect comparability with other providers as follows; TalkTalk is now comparable with EE.

Note: In Q4 2025, Sky and NOW Broadband's landline figures were resubmitted for Q3 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2025, Q2 2025, and Q3 2025. In Q3 2024, this resulted in a decrease in NOW Broadband's complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 8 to 7. This did not change NOW Broadband's position or comparability with other providers. In Q4 2024, this resulted in a decrease in NOW Broadband's complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 10 to 9. This did not change NOW Broadband's position or comparability with other providers.
Fixed broadband complaints per 100,000 customers/connections: Q4 2010 - Q1 2026, by quarter

Note: For Q1 2026, the actual measurable difference between the following fixed broadband providers' number of complaints per 100,000 customers was less than one and so their figures should be considered comparable:  1. Plusnet and Sky;  2. Sky, Virgin Media, EE and Industry Average;  3. Industry Average and BT; 4. BT and Vodafone.

Note: In Q2 2024, Vodafone resubmitted its broadband subscriber figures for Q3 2023, Q4 2023 and Q1 2024. In Q3 2023, this led to a small increase in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers and although the rounded overall number stayed static at 15, it moved down one position to be behind TalkTalk. In Q4 2023, this led to a small increase in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers, the rounded overall number stayed static at 14 and it remained in the same position. In Q1 2024, this led to a small increase in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers, the rounded overall number stayed static at 16, and it did not move position. In all 3 quarters, comparability with other providers was unchanged.

Note: In Q2 2023, Vodafone resubmitted its broadband subscriber figures for Q1 2023. This led to a small increase in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 16 to 17 in Q1 2023. This resulted in Vodafone moving down one position to behind Shell Energy and means that they were no longer comparable to Virgin Media in Q1 2023.

Note: Shell Energy purchased Post Office's telephony and broadband business in March 2021. From Q2 2021 onwards, complaints statistics for Shell Energy include complaints from a number of former Post Office customers who are served by Shell Energy.

Note: In Q4 2025, TalkTalk's Q3 2025 broadband subscriber figures were corrected. This resulted in no changes in their complaints per 100,000 subscribers. This did not change TalkTalk's position or comparability with other providers.

Note: In Q4 2025, Sky and NOW Broadband's broadband figures were resubmitted for Q3 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2025, Q2 2025, and Q3 2025. In Q4 2024, this resulted in a decrease in NOW Broadband's complaints per 100,000 from 15 to 13 and an increase in Sky's complaints per 100,000 from 5 to 6. This did not change NOW Broadband's position however, it did affect comparability with other providers as follows; NOW Broadband is now comparable with TalkTalk. This also did not change Sky's position or comparability with other providers.
Mobile pay monthly complaints per 100,000 customers/connections: Q1 2013 - Q1 2026, by quarter

Note: For Q1 2026, the actual measurable difference between the following pay-monthly mobile providers' number of complaints per 100,000 customers was less than one and so their figures should be considered comparable:  1. EE, Giffgaff, Vodafone, Three, Tesco Mobile and Industry Average; 2. Industry Average, O2 and iD Mobile.

Note: In Q1 2025, O2 resubmitted its mobile subscriber figures for Q2 2023, Q3 2023 and Q4 2023. In Q2 2023, this led to a small decrease in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 5 to 4. This resulted in O2 moving up one position and in front of iD Mobile and also becoming comparable to Vodafone, IA, Three and iD Mobile. In Q3 2023, this led to a small decrease in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 6 to 5. This resulted in O2 moving up one position and in front of BT and also becoming comparable to iD Mobile and Three. In Q4 2023 this led to a small decrease in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 7 to 6. This did not change O2's position or comparability with other providers.

Note: In Q3 2024, O2 resubmitted its mobile pay-monthly subscriber figures for Q1 2024 and Q2 2024. In both quarters, this led to a decrease in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 8 to 7, but it did not move position and was not comparable to any other providers.

Note: Vodafone pay monthly mobile complaints volumes and the industry average from Q4 2019 should not be compared with Vodafone pay monthly complaints volumes and the industry average prior to Q4 2019. This follows a methodological data improvement made in agreement with Ofcom, to how Vodafone records consumer and business tariff subscribers.
Note: For clarity we have stated Tesco Mobile's complaints per 100,000 customers/connections to one decimal place in Q2 2020.

Note: In Q4 2022, BT Mobile notified us that they had migrated onto a new system and as a result they resubmitted their subscriber figures for Q2 and Q3 2022. These changes did not affect their complaints per 100,000 subscribers after rounding, or their position in the league table for these two quarters. However it did affect their comparability with other providers as follows. In Q2 2022, Virgin Mobile was no longer comparable to BT Mobile, meaning that BT Mobile had the most complaints per 100,000 subscribers outright. And in Q3 2022, iD Mobile was no longer comparable to BT Mobile meaning that only Virgin Mobile and BT Mobile were the providers with the most complaints.

Note: In 2023, Virgin resubmitted its mobile pay-monthly subscriber figures for Q2 2023. This led to an increase in its complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 5 to 8 in Q2 2023. This resulted in Vodafone moving down one position to behind BT Mobile, who they are now comparable to as well as being no longer comparable to Three, iD Mobile and O2 in Q2 2023.
Pay TV complaints per 100,000 customers/connections: Q4 2011 - Q1 2026, by quarter

Note: For Q1 2026, the actual measurable difference between the following pay TV providers' number of complaints per 100,000 customers was less than one and so their figures should be considered comparable:  1. TalkTalk and Sky;  2. Sky, Industry Average and Virgin Media; 3. Virgin Media and EE.

Note: For Q1 2024, BT TV rebranded to EE TV in late 2023. As such, there is a possibility that some customers' complaints to us were still made under the BT brand rather than EE as the rebrand occurred.

Note: In Q4 2025, Sky resubmitted its pay TV subscriber figures for Q4 2023, Q1 2024, Q2 2024, Q3 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2025, Q2 2025, and Q3 2025. In Q2 2024, this led to a small increase in complaints per 100,000 subscribers from 1 to 2. This did not change Sky's position or comparability with other providers.
